newsitem.title: SWEDEN: UNICEF flying goods ex-Denmark to North Korea.
newsitem.headline: UNICEF flying goods ex-Denmark to North Korea.

text.p: The United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) said on Friday it flew about 15 tonnes of emergency supplies to North Korea in the past few weeks from its global purchasing and distribution centre in Copenhagen.
Ole Boye, shipping officer and emergency coordinator at UNICEF's supply division, told Reuters he expected to be sending more but that this would hinge on the availability of funds.
"I am quite certain we will be sending more because the country is in a state of dispair and there is an imminent need for food and hospital equipment," he said.
"This money would come from our usual government donors. I think they are appealing for money right now," Boye said.
Pyongyang has requested massive food assistance as a condition for joining proposed peace talks with South Korea, the United States and China.
Goods such as enriched baby formula, dried milk and pharmaceuticals are shipped regularly by sea or surface but an air lift is unusual and shows how critical the situation is, Boye said.
He said there was very little air freight capacity into the country.

"We have had difficulties shipping into North Korea, but have done so with a link through Bangkok. There is not much trade with North Korea so there is very little capacity in terms of ocean-going vessels or planes," Boye said.
North Korea was hit by unprecedented floods in 1995 and again in 1996, which devastated crops and caused food shortages that hunger experts say could lead to widespread famine this year.

The U.N. World Food Programme estimates North Korea needs 1.3 million tonnes of food to meet its basic needs this year. It has appealed for 200,000 tonnes of food worth $96 million, but has received only $38 million to date.
